qt: to the Commission Kristian Vigenin (S&D) Subject:

The death on 2 October 2026 of a worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute, a facility handling dangerous pathogens, remains unexplained. Whether an outbreak is natural, accidental or deliberate, the response is the same: identify the pathogen and deliver countermeasures fast. The ‘100 Days Mission’, an international goal endorsed by the G7 in 2021, aims for deployable countermeasures within 100 days of identifying a novel pathogen. It is a biosecurity tool as much as a public health one. The medical countermeasures strategy commits the Commission to step up civil-military cooperation, and biological countermeasures are already being developed with EU defence funding. In the light of the above: 1.
Will the Commission integrate the 100 Days Mission as a pillar of the EU’s biosecurity policy, and does it consider funding through research work programmes alone to be sufficient?

Are the results of defence-funded countermeasure research, and the resulting countermeasures, made available to the Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Authority, civilian researchers and civilian stockpiles, or do classification rules keep them within defence ministries?

Is the Commission planning to commit more of the funds from Horizon Europe 2028– 2034 to international partnerships and neglected diseases with epidemic potential, so that threats are contained before they reach the EU?
